column3: Directly frames guidance as placement on the straight path.
Pairs being guided with entry onto a praiseworthy path.
States being on a straight path, though it does not name the guiding act.
Directly describes divine guidance onto a straight path.
Begins the immediate account of divine favor to Moses and Aaron.
Its more upright speech offers only a distant resonance with sustained rectitude.
An upright measure illustrates rectitude but not guidance or a route.
The refusal to remember does not clarify the guidance of Moses and Aaron.
Connects belief and humbled hearts to divine guidance onto a straight path.
Shows the straight path as a site of obstruction, a useful contrast to successful guidance.
Holding fast to Allah results in being guided onto a straight path.
Closely parallels the focus by guiding a selected plural group onto a straight path.
Links belonging to the sound path with having received guidance.
Continues the immediate Moses-and-Aaron sequence by naming their rescue and that of their people.
Embodies the contrast between disoriented movement and upright walking on a straight path.
Shows that speed cannot yield direction when sight and the path trace are removed.
The call to remember belongs to another local subchannel and adds no route guidance.
Its sustaining social provision gives only a secondary resonance with what keeps people upright.
The upright scale illustrates just measure rather than the guided route itself.
Exempts devoted servants from Satan's reach, contrasting protection with path obstruction.
Presents the Quran as guiding toward what is most upright.
Explicitly joins clear signs with divine guidance onto a straight path.
Continues the immediate account by reporting the divinely granted victory.
Names revelation as light and the messenger as one who guides to a straight path.
Defines rejection of the hereafter as swerving away from the path.
The recitation of remembrance does not add to the guidance statement.
Establishing revealed scripture broadly supports the revealed basis of a straight course.
Asks for guidance to the middle of the path, adding a judicial image of straightness.
Immediately precedes the focus by giving Moses and Aaron the clarifying Book.
Calls the divine way straight, but does not add the focus's guided recipients.
Portrays guidance as making alternative ascents discernible.
The description of the drink in Paradise does not clarify the route.
Withholds guidance from defiantly corrupt people, providing a limited negative boundary.
Directly describes the messenger's call to a straight path.
Includes Moses within the undivided continuity of received revelation.
Links a contested change of orientation to divine guidance onto a straight path.
Guides Abraham, a grateful chosen recipient, onto a straight path.
The wish for an earlier reminder does not elucidate the focus.
Identifies worship of the one Lord as the straight path.
Uses guidance toward a path in a contrary, punitive direction.
Shows revealed light leading from darkness through paths of peace to a straight path.
Calls the revelation guidance for believers without adding the route image.
Carving rock in the valley has no material connection to guidance onto a path.
Connects faith and holding fast with mercy and guidance to a straight path toward Allah.
Relates upright religion to setting one's face in the proper direction.
Pairs the call to the abode of peace with guidance to a straight path.
The Paradise drink description does not clarify the focus.
Defines worship of Allah as the straight path.
Repeats the worship-as-straight-path formulation already supplied more fully.
The description of sheltered companions does not bear on guidance.
Its language of sustaining responsibility only indirectly resonates with upright support.
The speaker explicitly reports being guided by his Lord to a straight, upright religion.
The question about angels does not clarify the route or its guidance.
Associates uncorrupted faith with security and being rightly guided, without a path formulation.
Contrasts darkness and misguidance with being placed on a straight path.
Depicts active blocking and bending of Allah's path, clarifying the danger guidance overcomes.
Leaving the standing messenger for commerce does not clarify the focus.
A prophet offers to guide his father to an even path.
The image of the tree's fruit does not add to guidance onto the straight path.
Places guidance to disputed truth within revelation and ends with a straight-path formulation.
Names divine guidance of the messenger to a straight path after favor is completed.
Specifies that the straight path belongs to Allah and that all affairs return to Him.
Divine self-subsistence offers a remote support resonance but no guided-route relation.
Shows guidance of a community to a straight path after protection from hostile hands.
Following ancestral traces does not clarify the Moses-and-Aaron guidance.
Balanced spending gives only a secondary image of sustaining uprightness.
Connects recognition of revelation as truth with guidance to the path of the Mighty, Praised One.
Contrasts ineffective dependence with justice while standing on a straight path.
Makes holding fast to revelation the means of remaining on a straight path.
Affirms that guidance belongs to Allah but adds no route or recipient detail.
Marks devoted servants as outside Satan's authority, a limited boundary for guidance.
Attributes the favor of being guided to faith to Allah rather than human merit.
The bare naming of Abraham's and Lot's peoples adds no route relation.
Supplies the light and clear Book that the following verse develops as guidance.
Moses' people turn aside despite knowing him, contrasting rejection with his guided community's fate.
The fasting regulations do not clarify the focus's path guidance.
Commands following Abraham's upright creed, extending a received course across prophets.
Its stabilizing sacred institutions only indirectly echo the focus's sustaining route.
States that guidance makes a way known while leaving the human response open.
The warning to an unwarned people does not add to the focus's guided route.
Distinguishes guided descendants from transgressors within prophetic inheritance.
Contrasts the straight intended way with a deviating way and assigns its direction to Allah.
The warning's ineffectiveness does not clarify the focus's guidance.
Establishing prayer gives only a secondary image of maintaining an upright order.
Describes a message that guides to right conduct and elicits belief.
Commands following Abraham's upright religious course.
Persistent justice offers an indirect image of upright conduct, not a guided path.
The emergence of pearls and coral has no connection to the focus.
The statement of widespread misguidance adds no distinct route insight after earlier contrasts.
Links obedience to the messenger with receiving guidance.
The raised roof has no material relation to the focus.
Critiques inherited following when it lacks understanding and guidance.
An enduring traveled road is a physical route image without the focus's guidance relation.
Pharaoh's claim to guide to right conduct supplies a contrast between asserted and divine guidance.
Describes prophetic accounts as guidance and mercy in a broad, non-route sense.
Tests whether someone can find guidance after a familiar object is altered.
Inheritance apportionment does not clarify guidance onto the straight path.
Abraham's movement toward his Lord is coupled with expectation of forthcoming guidance.
Its repeated hady concerns sacrificial offerings rather than guidance.
Prepared earth and its paths provide a broad physical model for finding guidance.
Continues the immediate Moses-and-Aaron account by preserving their honored remembrance.
Directly names peace upon Moses and Aaron, completing the focus's prophetic pair.
Explains their treatment as the reward given to those who do good.
Identifies Moses and Aaron as believing servants, completing the sequence that contains the focus.
Explicitly gives Moses and Aaron the Book so that they might be guided.
Directly calls the Lord's way straight and ties it to explained signs.
Directly declares Allah's path straight and commands following it rather than divergent ways.
Describes the Lord as being upon a straight path, grounding the path in divine justice and governance.
Makes following divine guidance the condition for avoiding error and misery.
Distinguishes human desire to guide from Allah's decisive knowledge of who receives guidance.
Connects the Book given to Moses with guidance for the Children of Israel.
Links safety from punishment to following guidance in the Moses-and-Pharaoh encounter.
States that the Creator both gives each thing its form and then guides it.
Portrays prophetic leaders as guiding by divine command and enacting upright works.
Shows Moses being given a traversable route through the sea during liberation.
Describes Israelite leaders guiding by divine command after patience and certainty.
Defines revelation as bringing people from darkness into light by their Lord's permission.
Places guidance and misguidance within the repeated prophetic call to worship Allah alone.
Names the Book given to Moses as guidance for the Children of Israel.
States that Allah's guidance is decisive and that none can guide one left astray.
The covenant not to worship Satan supplies the negative side of the worship-path command in the next ayah.
Presents the Book as the means by which Allah guides those receptive to His guidance.
Contrasts Pharaoh's claim with the believer's offer to guide his people to the path of right conduct.
Connects revealed religion, prophetic continuity, and the command to remain upright in it.
Again defines worship of the one Lord as the straight path.
Describes a confirming Book after Moses that guides to truth and a straight path.
